classification.difficultyReason: Complete non-monic squares, determine exact intercepts and combine the features in sketches.

content.prompt:
For each parabola:

i determine the $y$-intercept

ii complete the square

iii find the axis of symmetry and the vertex

iv determine any $x$-intercepts

v sketch the parabola

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=3$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=2(x^2+2x)+3\\y&=2[(x+1)^2-1]+3\\y&=2(x+1)^2+1\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-1$ and the vertex is $(-1,1)$. Since $y\geq1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,3)$ with minimum $(-1,1)$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with vertex, y-intercept and dashed symmetry axis; no x-intercepts.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=7$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(x^2+2x)+7\\y&=-2[(x+1)^2-1]+7\\y&=-2(x+1)^2+9\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-1$ and the vertex is $(-1,9)$.

For the $x$-intercepts:

$$\begin{align*}0&=-2(x+1)^2+9\\2(x+1)^2&=9\\(x+1)^2&=\frac92\\x+1&=\pm\frac{3\sqrt2}{2}\\x&=\frac{-2\pm3\sqrt2}{2}\end{align*}$$

Sketch a downward-opening parabola through these intercepts with maximum $(-1,9)$.

spec.description: Complete downward-opening solution graph with both exact x-intercepts, y-intercept, vertex and symmetry axis.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=-19$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=3(x^2+4x)-19\\y&=3[(x+2)^2-4]-19\\y&=3(x+2)^2-31\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-2$ and the vertex is $(-2,-31)$.

For the $x$-intercepts:

$$\begin{align*}0&=3(x+2)^2-31\\3(x+2)^2&=31\\(x+2)^2&=\frac{31}{3}\\x+2&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{93}}3\\x&=\frac{-6\pm\sqrt{93}}3\end{align*}$$

Sketch an upward-opening parabola through these intercepts with minimum $(-2,-31)$.

spec.description: Complete upward-opening solution sketch with exact intercepts and minimum.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=-2$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=3\left(x^2+\frac83x\right)-2\\y&=3\left[\left(x+\frac43\right)^2-\frac{16}9\right]-2\\y&=3\left(x+\frac43\right)^2-\frac{22}3\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-\frac43$ and the vertex is $\left(-\frac43,-\frac{22}3\right)$.

For the $x$-intercepts:

$$\begin{align*}0&=3\left(x+\frac43\right)^2-\frac{22}3\\3\left(x+\frac43\right)^2&=\frac{22}3\\\left(x+\frac43\right)^2&=\frac{22}9\\x+\frac43&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{22}}3\\x&=\frac{-4\pm\sqrt{22}}3\end{align*}$$

Sketch an upward-opening parabola through these intercepts with the stated minimum.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch retaining fractional vertex and exact radical intercepts.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=-15$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=2\left(x^2+\frac12x\right)-15\\y&=2\left[\left(x+\frac14\right)^2-\frac1{16}\right]-15\\y&=2\left(x+\frac14\right)^2-\frac{121}8\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-\frac14$ and the vertex is $\left(-\frac14,-\frac{121}8\right)$.

For the $x$-intercepts:

$$\begin{align*}0&=2\left(x+\frac14\right)^2-\frac{121}8\\2\left(x+\frac14\right)^2&=\frac{121}8\\\left(x+\frac14\right)^2&=\frac{121}{16}\\x+\frac14&=\pm\frac{11}4\\x&=-3\text{ or }\frac52\end{align*}$$

Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-3,0)$, $\left(\frac52,0\right)$ and $(0,-15)$ with the stated minimum.

spec.description: Complete solution graph; a leader separates the vertex label from the nearby y-intercept.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=5$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=2\left(x^2-\frac12x\right)+5\\y&=2\left[\left(x-\frac14\right)^2-\frac1{16}\right]+5\\y&=2\left(x-\frac14\right)^2+\frac{39}8\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=\frac14$ and the vertex is $\left(\frac14,\frac{39}8\right)$. Since $y\geq\frac{39}8>0$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,5)$ with the stated minimum.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with minimum above the x-axis; leader separates vertex and y-intercept labels.
